messages:
maria (arch): quick RFC follow-up — marking down an alternative to staged bundles: 'patchlets' approach. small signed deltas that apply on top of an immutable base image, verified by a lightweight sidecar. thoughts?

ajay (eng-platform): sounds interesting — how are patchlets different from our delta bundles?

maria (arch): two main diffs: 1) patchlets are tiny (MBs) and composable, not a single large delta; 2) they carry apply metadata so operator can apply in any order and still reach a consistent state.

ben (eng-runtime): composable is appealing for model shards. worry: KV-cache & hot GPU memory consistency during concurrent patchlet applies. we need a safe quiesce or streaming rebase.

maria (arch): agree. proposal: sidecar exposes an apply API that can do: PREPARE -> STREAM_APPLY -> COMMIT. PREPARE reserves cache slots, STREAM_APPLY sends chunked patchlet, COMMIT swaps pointers atomically.

sophie (sec): signing/attestation is mandatory. patchlets must include chain of signatures up to release key and an allowlist for operator identity. also replay protection (nonce/epoch).

ajay (eng-platform): operator handshake idea: operator receives manifest with list of patchlets + apply order hints. operator must ACK manifest before sidecars start PREPARE. allows orchestrated rollouts.

maria (arch): exactly. manifest snippet idea: 
```
patchlets: [
  {id: "m-0001", url: "s3://...", sig: "base64", epoch: 202503},
  {id: "w-0002", url: "s3://...", sig: "base64", epoch: 202503}
]
order_hints: ["m-0001","w-0002"]
```

ben (eng-runtime): runtime notes: to avoid tail latency spikes we should do a streaming apply that updates a shadow KV index and then atomically swap the active index on COMMIT. prewarming shard pages needed.

sophie (sec): what about offline/air-gapped installs where S3 isn't reachable? we still need to support USB/tarballs. patchlets must be transport-agnostic (content-addressed).

maria (arch): yep — transport-agnostic. patchlet = (meta + content) where content is content-addressed chunk set. operator can deliver via registry, USB, or sidecar fetch proxy.

nina (prod): rollback story? if COMMIT fails mid-apply, how do we surface and recover without full base reimage?

maria (arch): two options: 1) apply-idempotent patchlets so partial stream is safe to resume; 2) maintain a per-node activation log and on failure run a revert patchlet that undoes committed changes (we publish revert patchlets alongside each patchlet).

ben (eng-runtime): revert patchlets are good but heavy. prefer resumable chunking + apply watermarking + GC of incomplete artifacts. sidecar should expose a `resume_token` for partial streams.

ajay (eng-platform): rollout and safety: operator supports canary -> ramp -> global. operator enforces max_concurrent_applies/per-region and fallbacks to previous model variant if too many COMMIT aborts.

sophie (sec): auditability: every PREPARE/COMMIT/REVERT must be logged to immutable audit (KMS-signed event) and surfaced in Console.

devops-bot: deploy-check: manifest schema validated, signatures ok, region quotas ok.

maria (arch): perf tradeoffs: more, smaller patchlets increases parallelism and reduces bundle churn but raises overhead of verification and metadata. we should run microbenchmarks: small patchlet throughput vs large delta throughput.

ben (eng-runtime): test matrix suggestion: model shard sizes [10MB, 100MB, 1GB], concurrency [1,4,16], resume vs full replace. measure tail latency, COMMIT latency, and memory overhead.

nina (prod): UX ask: operator should provide a dry-run mode that simulates PREPARE + STREAM_APPLY without COMMIT to validate resources. also a preview in Console showing estimated bandwidth and apply window.

maria (arch): ok action items: 1) I'll draft a mini-RFC that outlines manifest, sidecar API (PREPARE/STREAM_APPLY/COMMIT/REVERT/STATUS), and signature chain. 2) ben + team to prototype streaming apply & shadow KV swap. 3) sophie to write signing/nonce requirements. 4) ajay to spec operator manifest ACK and concurrency controls.

ajay (eng-platform): timeline?

maria (arch): aim for prototype in 3 weeks, benchmark week after, RFC final in 6 weeks.

sophie (sec): acked — will carve out time.

ben (eng-runtime): ack, I'll spin up a small harness for shard resume tests.

nina (prod): love the dry-run idea. put me on the follow-up UX thread.

maria (arch): thanks all. filing the mini-RFC now, pinging in #eng-runtime when done. :white_check_mark:
